chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Indeed, if the person in ihram marries while he is in ihram, they are separated, and they never remarry each other again." If he was unaware of the prohibition of that, it is permissible for him to contract marriage with her after exiting ihram. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْإِحْلَالُ: Exiting the state of ihram / becoming permissible again
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.فُرِّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا: They were separated / the marriage was dissolved

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage contracted by a person while in the state of ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the ruling of *firqah* (separation without divorce) for a muhrim who marries, preventing the couple from remarrying each other unless they undergo a new contract. The hadith distinguishes between intentional violation and ignorance (*ghayr 'alim*), noting that if the muhrim was unaware of the prohibition, the contract remains valid upon exiting ihram, reflecting the Shia principle that ignorance can mitigate legal consequences. This ruling is central to the jurisprudence of Hajj, emphasizing the sanctity of the pilgrim's state while accommodating human error.
